A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Few-Class Arena and SimSS. Their main texts, appendices, equations, tables, and figures are readable and support reliable comparison despite reformatting and added experiments.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification experiments, full-model versus subset-model evaluations, and analyses relating SimSS to accuracy across datasets and architectures.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds fine-tuning comparisons and COCO object-detection and segmentation results.

M1.justification: The configurable subset loading, FC-Full, FC-Sub, and CLIP/DINOv2-based SimSS procedures are retained. Appendix A.9 elaborates nearest-class selection for each instance, an operation already described in v1, rather than establishing a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: The ten classification datasets remain. v2 Appendix A.12 adds actual COCO object-detection and segmentation evaluations at 2, 5, and 80 classes, substantially extending coverage beyond image classification.

E2.justification: v2 introduces fine-tuned comparators alongside full and subset-trained models. Section 4.4 evaluates fine-tuned ResNet18, ResNet50, MobileViT-small, and CLIP-initialized ViT-B on CIFAR100; Table 8 also compares full, fine-tuned, and subset-trained YOLOv8-nano models. The original ten-model comparison remains.

E3.justification: New protocols include 100-epoch CIFAR100 full-model training followed by 20-epoch fine-tuning, and a CLIP-initialized ViT-B with an added linear layer trained for 10 epochs. COCO experiments introduce 320x320 inputs, mAP@50 evaluation, and five-epoch fine-tuning. Original dataset splits and the retained training-parameter table are unchanged.

E4.justification: Fine-tuning comparisons add controls testing whether the full-versus-subset conclusions persist under transfer learning. Conversely, v1's entire ViT-versus-SimSS analysis and Figure 20 disappear. Figure 18(a)'s class-count sensitivity analysis is also narrowed by removing two plotted settings.

E5.justification: Both retain the five-subset default with seeds 0-4, subset-variability reporting, and Pearson correlations with p-values. The added STDEV columns continue existing variability reporting; no increased repeat count or changed statistical estimation procedure is documented.

E6.justification: New tables report fine-tuning, architecture summaries, and COCO outcomes; Table 8 gives two-class detection mAP@50 of 0.488, 0.505, and 0.538 for full, fine-tuned, and subset-trained models. v1's ViT-SimSS correlations of 0.12-0.20 are removed, as are Figure 18(a)'s Caltech256 NCL=154 and CIFAR100 NCL=20 points. Table 1 and the headline Figure 5 correlations remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The similarity definitions and SimSS derivation in Equations (1)-(14) retain their mathematical substance. Nearest-class notation and explanatory wording are clarified, without a new theorem, proof, assumption, or substantive derivation change.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims about FCA, scalable subset loading, SimSS, strong ResNet correlations, and class-count scaling behavior. Additional experiments support these claims without materially redefining the stated contributions.

C2.justification: v2 extends the feature-specialization explanation to pretrained and fine-tuned models and interprets the new task comparisons as supporting similar few-class behavior. It removes the explicit ViT-SimSS failure discussion and the training-scheduler convergence caveat, changing the disclosed applicability boundaries. Representation similarity is added as a future direction.

D1.justification: v2 adds practitioner/researcher usage guidance, explicit nearest-class selection instructions, and an additional RTX 3090 Ti computing setup. It changes the stated repository from fewclassarena/fca to bryanbocao/fca and revises several dataset-license entries. Existing data-format instructions, splits, and optimizer details remain.

R1.justification: New Appendix A.3 substantially expands positioning against few-shot and self-supervised learning, adding literature on data scarcity, contrastive learning, and masked autoencoders. The conclusion adds representation-similarity research, while v1's cited classification-difficulty paper by Cao and colleagues is removed. These changes extend beyond citation-format conversion.

P1.justification: Most original exposition remains closely matched. Changes include localized wording corrections, expanded nearest-class explanations, revised author information, and moving Goals from Section 3.1 to Appendix A.1. New sections are inserted without wholesale rewriting of the existing narrative.

P2.justification: The document adopts ICLR formatting with different text width, title and author layout, headers, and extensive display relocation and resizing. It adds Tables 2, 7, and 8, removes Figure 20, revises Figure 18(a)'s axis and curves, and corrects Figure 4's reversed color descriptions.

improvement.justification: Fine-tuning controls, COCO evaluations, and usage guidance address practical gaps in v1. However, removing Figure 20 eliminates evidence that SimSS correlates poorly with ViT accuracy, an important qualification of the central difficulty metric; the convergence caveat also disappears. Broader validation and better guidance coexist with less complete disclosure of limitations, preventing a confident net quality judgment.
